boundaryQuestions.question: Does oven_heating_system survive as one functional abstraction, or do bake/broil/convection require separate canonical concepts or instance scopes?
Is surface_heating_system diagnostically sufficient, or does electric-element vs infinite-switch vs bridge-element architecture require finer canonical decomposition?
Does one temperature_sensor abstraction work across manufacturers for oven cavity feedback?
Is convection_fan consistently canonical, and does its diagnostic relationship to oven heating matter at canonical level?
Does thermal_protection remain functional like refrigerator conditionals, or do fuse/cutout/limit architectures imply different diagnostic roles?
Can electric/gas/induction/dual-fuel eventually share one range/oven functional contract, or does electric discovery prove split ontologies are required?

immutableRules: CG-10 is discovery only — candidate graph may be deleted, merged, split, or rejected by manual evidence.
Success includes proving the candidate wrong — not defending the hypothesis skeleton.
No writes to frontend/components/diagnostics/knowledge/canonical/ except via future human freeze gate after R1+R2+R3.
No gate tables, no overlay publish, no compounding in CG-10.
Procedure seeds and CG-3 normalization inform observations — they do not auto-promote candidate concepts.
Refrigerator family lock remains authoritative — no refrigerator ontology reopen from range discovery.
